issues.legal_issue: The custodian cannot be required to evict occupants and deliver vacant possession of property leased or allotted by the custodian unless a permitted ground for eviction exists.
material_facts: The mortgagee’s interest in the mortgaged property vested in the custodian after the mortgagee was declared an evacuee.
The custodian took possession and let or allotted the property to occupants.
The custodian refused the mortgagor’s requests to remove those occupants and give him vacant possession.
The case did not establish a ground for eviction under rent-control law or a breach of the occupants’ lease or allotment conditions.
issues.conclusion: The custodian could not be required to deliver vacant possession by evicting occupants except on a ground permitted by the applicable rules governing the custodian’s leases and allotments.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Administration of Evacuee Property Act, 1950 gives that Act overriding effect, so ordinary rights under the Transfer of Property Act do not override the statutory scheme. Sections 8, 10 and 12 of the Administration Act give the custodian control over evacuee property, while rule 14 of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950 limits eviction of occupants under leases or allotments granted by the custodian to permitted rent-control grounds, breaches of the lease or allotment, and the further grounds specified by that rule. The custodian is not subject to the control of the competent officer under the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951.

predicates.evacuee_property_under_custodian_control: The property or an interest in it has vested in the authority administering evacuee property.
predicates.occupants_hold_custodian_leases_or_allot: The custodian has let or allotted the property to occupants.
predicates.permitted_eviction_ground: A ground permitted by the rules governing the custodian’s leases or allotments for evicting the occupants exists.

issues.definition: When property is under evacuee-property administration, occupants hold leases or allotments granted by the custodian, and no permitted eviction ground exists, the custodian cannot be required to give vacant possession.

issues.legal_issue: A competent officer cannot order the custodian to deliver vacant possession of mortgaged property without the custodian’s agreement.
material_facts: The mortgagor sought to pay the mortgage debt and obtain vacant possession of the property.
The custodian had placed tenants or allottees in the property and did not agree to deliver vacant possession.
The mortgagor’s mortgage claim was dealt with by a competent officer under the separation scheme.
issues.conclusion: Without an agreement between the custodian and the mortgagor, the competent officer could not order redemption with vacant possession or direct the custodian to remove the occupants; at most, the officer could direct symbolic possession.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 7, 8 and 10 of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 provide for claims concerning composite property and empower the competent officer to separate interests, including by paying the mortgage debt, redeeming the property, selling it or partitioning it. Section 10 makes those powers subject to rules. Rule 11B(b) of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Rules permits redemption or partition where the custodian and claimant agree, and otherwise provides for sale to satisfy the mortgage debt. The Separation Act does not make the custodian subject to the competent officer’s control or empower that officer to cancel the custodian’s leases or allotments. Rule 14 of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950 independently restricts eviction of occupants. The Court noted the hardship of this result and referred to The All India Film Corporation Ltd. v. Raja Gyan Nath, [1970] 2 S.C.R. 581.

predicates.separation_proceeding_involving_mortgage: A proceeding to separate interests concerns property subject to a mortgage and containing both evacuee and non-evacuee interests.
predicates.custodian_has_placed_occupants_in_proper: The custodian has let or allotted the property to occupants.
predicates.custodian_agrees_to_vacant_possession: The custodian has agreed to deliver the property free of its occupants.

issues.definition: In a proceeding to separate interests in mortgaged composite property, if the custodian has placed occupants there and has not agreed to vacant possession, the competent officer cannot order vacant possession.

issues.legal_issue: A sale order made to satisfy a mortgage debt is valid when the debt remains unpaid because the mortgagor conditioned payment on receiving vacant possession that the competent officer could not require the custodian to provide.
material_facts: The competent officer determined the mortgage debt and ordered the property sold to satisfy it.
The mortgagor repeatedly offered to pay only if he received vacant possession at the same time.
There was no agreement between the mortgagor and the custodian for delivery of vacant possession.
The mortgagor had not actually paid or tendered the mortgage debt when the sale order was made and confirmed.
issues.conclusion: The sale order was valid in the circumstances existing when it was made, because the debt remained outstanding and the mortgagor could not insist on payment being exchanged for vacant possession.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 10 of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 requires the competent officer to accept a mortgagor’s tender of the amount due in full satisfaction of the mortgage debt. However, the officer’s powers under section 10 are subject to the rules, and rule 11B(b) of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Rules does not permit redemption with vacant possession without the custodian’s agreement. Where the mortgage debt remains unpaid, the competent officer may order sale for its satisfaction and distribution of the proceeds. The judgment also referred to Ek Nawas Khan v. The Competent Officer, A.I.R. 1960 All. 626, in connection with the position of an auction purchaser.

rule.if: appeal_against_mortgage_sale_order and mortgage_debt_unpaid_when_sale_order_made and payment_conditioned_on_unavailable_vacant_possession and not custodian_agrees_to_vacant_possession

predicates.appeal_against_mortgage_sale_order: The proceeding challenges an order for sale of mortgaged property to satisfy the mortgage debt.
predicates.mortgage_debt_unpaid_when_sale_order_mad: The mortgage debt had not been paid or actually tendered when the sale order was made.
predicates.payment_conditioned_on_unavailable_vacan: The mortgagor offered to pay only on condition of receiving vacant possession that the competent officer could not order.
predicates.custodian_agrees_to_vacant_possession: The custodian has agreed to deliver the property free of its occupants.

issues.definition: In an appeal against a mortgage-sale order, if the debt remained unpaid, payment was conditioned on vacant possession that could not be ordered, and the custodian had not agreed to deliver vacant possession, the sale order was valid when made.

issues.legal_issue: A sale order made only to satisfy a mortgage debt must be set aside if the debt is later paid in full and the payment is accepted.
material_facts: After the competent officer and appellate officer had ordered and confirmed a sale, the mortgagor paid the entire mortgage debt.
The competent officer accepted the full payment.
The mortgage debt was therefore no longer outstanding when the Supreme Court considered the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The sale order had become untenable because the mortgage debt had been satisfied, and it had to be set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 10(b)(ii) of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951, the competent officer may sell mortgaged property for satisfaction of the mortgage debt and distribute the proceeds. The proviso to section 10 requires acceptance of the mortgagor’s tender in full satisfaction of that debt. Once the debt has been paid and accepted, there is no remaining debt for a sale under section 10(b)(ii) to satisfy.

rule.if: appeal_against_mortgage_sale_order and sale_order_made_to_satisfy_mortgage_debt and full_debt_paid_after_order and payment_accepted

predicates.appeal_against_mortgage_sale_order: The proceeding challenges an order for sale of mortgaged property to satisfy the mortgage debt.
predicates.sale_order_made_to_satisfy_mortgage_debt: The competent officer ordered sale for the purpose of satisfying the mortgage debt.
predicates.full_debt_paid_after_order: The mortgagor paid the entire mortgage debt after the sale order was made.
predicates.payment_accepted: The competent officer accepted the payment in satisfaction of the mortgage debt.

issues.definition: If an order for sale to satisfy a mortgage debt is under appeal and the full debt has since been paid and accepted, the sale order must be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: After accepting full payment of the mortgage debt, the competent officer must direct symbolic possession but cannot direct vacant possession without the custodian’s agreement.
material_facts: The mortgagor paid the full mortgage debt after the sale order was made, and the competent officer accepted it.
The custodian had placed occupants in the property and had not agreed to deliver vacant possession.
The mortgagor sought possession of the property after the mortgage debt had been satisfied.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage was discharged and the competent officer was bound to direct symbolic possession to the mortgagor, but could not order the custodian to give vacant possession.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 10 of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Act, 1951 requires the competent officer to accept a mortgagor’s tender in full satisfaction of the mortgage debt. Section 10 makes the competent officer’s powers subject to the rules, and rule 11B(b) of the Evacuee Interest (Separation) Rules prevents redemption with vacant possession in the absence of the custodian’s agreement. The competent officer cannot use section 10 to cancel or vary leases or allotments granted by the custodian; rule 14 of the Administration of Evacuee Property (Central) Rules, 1950 restricts the custodian’s power to evict occupants. The resulting direction may therefore be limited to symbolic possession.

rule.if: separation_proceeding_involving_mortgaged_composite_property and full_debt_paid_and_accepted and custodian_has_placed_occupants_in_property and not custodian_agrees_to_vacant_possession

predicates.separation_proceeding_involving_mortgage: A proceeding to separate interests concerns property subject to a mortgage and containing both evacuee and non-evacuee interests.
predicates.full_debt_paid_and_accepted: The mortgagor has paid the full mortgage debt and the competent officer has accepted that payment.
predicates.custodian_has_placed_occupants_in_proper: The custodian has let or allotted the property to occupants.
predicates.custodian_agrees_to_vacant_possession: The custodian has agreed to deliver the property free of its occupants.

issues.definition: In a separation proceeding, if the full mortgage debt has been paid and accepted, the custodian has placed occupants in the property, and the custodian has not agreed to vacant possession, the competent officer must direct symbolic possession only.
